advantages.what: A damaged data file does not print the saved provider token to the server output
Unwritable or damaged data folder stops startup with a plain message and a recovery step instead of a raw stack trace
Bots with the same name are told apart by a stable Bot #n and conversation label, visually and by description
A lookup of ORD-1001A gets a notice that the identifier could not be used and how to correct it, not ORD-1001's value
After a refused rename the instruction form is not left silently bound to the edited entry, so no saved entry is lost
Proposed values are validated (non-numeric totals, unknown fields, decimal creates refused with correction guidance) instead of applying 'total: 125 -> banana'
Field names match regardless of capitals with the same value and preview (Z refuses with guidance)
Tests catch a broken DATA_DIR default and per-conversation memory filtering, which Z's suite misses
After a storage write failure a pending reply is marked failed with Retry instead of blocking the conversation
A storage failure during a task marks only that task Failed with Retry task; Y puts the whole app into a 503 mode, reads included, until an operator restarts it
The instruction in force is shown with its text and a Clear instructions button
Cross-tier submission-receipt protocol, strict snapshot validator, re-parsed stand-in grammar and a shipped acceptance/ harness are extra code a maintainer must carry

lesser_lacks: Catch damaged or unwritable data at startup and print a plain message naming the problem and the recovery step, never the file contents or token (D-2, D-3)
Distinguish same-named bots in the Bots navigation (number or description) or refuse duplicates (D-4)
Add a notice when a typed record id such as ORD-1001A does not exist instead of passing through ORD-1001's value (D-6)
Clear the instruction/task form binding after a refused rename so a new entry is not saved over the edited one (D-13)
Validate proposed values (numeric totals, existing fields) with correction guidance before offering a proposal (U-30)
pairs.why: Y avoids five defects Z has, including the token printed to the server output and silent loss of a saved instruction, and it also validates proposed values. Z handles storage failures more gracefully (D-11, D-12) and shows the active instruction, but those cover rarer conditions. Y's heavier send protocol and shipped harness cost the maintainer something, though not enough to reverse the balance.

advantages.what: Keyboard Confirm/Reject moves focus to Message, so a second Enter cannot decide another proposal
A capitalised field name in a change request is refused with the right field named, instead of creating a second Status field in the record
Conversations are distinguishable before opening (numbered duplicates, tooltip with latest message)
After a storage write failure the pending reply is marked failed with Retry, not left pending until restart
A storage failure during a task marks it Failed with Retry task instead of Running forever
Saving under an existing name without Edit is refused with a message instead of silently overwriting
README tells many of the decided behaviours (duplicate saves, forget matching, Since you were away, storage failures, field capitals)
21 tests against X's 8; Z's suite catches a server-side break of token refusal that X's does not test

lesser_lacks: Stop focus restoration by accessible name from landing on another proposal's Confirm/Reject button (D-8)
Match or refuse field names in other capitals so a change never creates a second field (D-9)
Give empty and similar conversations distinct labels or descriptions (D-10)
Mark an in-flight reply failed with Retry when its progress cannot be saved (D-11)
Mark a task Failed with Retry task when its step progress cannot be saved (D-12)
Refuse or announce saving an instruction or task under an existing name (D-14)
pairs.why: Both meet the stated requirements, but X carries six more defects, four of them medium. Two put records at risk: a keyboard Enter can confirm the wrong proposal, and a capitalised field silently splits a record. X shows no advantage over Z, and fixing its storage-failure paths and focus handling is more than one short task.

advantages.what: No token printed to the server output on a damaged data file
Plain startup refusal with a recovery step for damaged or unwritable data
Same-named bots distinguishable
Suffixed record id gets a correction notice rather than another record's value
Keyboard decision moves focus to that proposal's Change result, never to another proposal's button
Field names are case-insensitive, so no stray second field is created
Conversations get distinguishing labels and chat numbers
No silent loss of an instruction after a refused rename
Duplicate saved names are refused rather than silently overwritten
Proposed values validated with correction guidance
19 tests that catch a broken DATA_DIR default and memory scoping, which X's 8 miss
A task storage failure leaves the rest of the app readable, while Y switches the whole app to 503 until restart (both still leave the reply and task stuck)
Simpler code without Y's cross-tier receipt protocol and shipped acceptance harness

lesser_lacks: Plain startup error for damaged or unwritable data without the file contents or token (D-2, D-3)
Distinguish same-named bots and similar conversations (D-4, D-10)
Notice for a nonexistent suffixed record id (D-6)
Fix focus after keyboard Confirm/Reject so it never lands on another proposal (D-8)
Clear the form binding after a refused rename and refuse or announce duplicate saved names (D-13, D-14)
Validate proposed values with correction guidance (U-30)
pairs.why: Y avoids nine defects X has, including the two that can change records the person did not mean to change (D-8, D-9) and the token printed to the server output. X's only gains are a smaller codebase and a less drastic reaction to storage failure. The gap covers many separate fixes on both server and client.
